latest_command_review.scope: Compared Script.cpp/Script.h registrations at current upstream master: the same 40 commands. Reviewed SessionData tunnel, local-browser and workspace surfaces at the pinned baseline. This is not a full behavior review of upstream master.

verification.policy: A status of 'verified' means the behavior was checked, not that it looked right while somebody was reading the code. So an entry carries 'verified_on': for each platform LinSCP ships on, the suites whose tests cover it. LinSCP ships on Linux alone - the Windows port was removed - so an entry may be 'verified' only when 'linux' appears in that map naming the suites that actually ran it. The rule is still written for any number of platforms, and a suite that is not listed under a platform cannot be cited for it, because evidence nobody can reproduce is not evidence. The notes stay authoritative about what is missing either way - evidence for the parts that are covered does not certify the rest, which is why --require-full fails while any entry is not verified.

linux.how: make -C source/linux all check && make -C source/linux check-live (the same suites also run under CMake/CTest: cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build); dpkg-buildpackage -b -us -uc builds the .deb that CI installs; `make -C source/linux check-live` includes the browser upload regression suite; npm install --no-save --package-lock=false jsdom@29 && node source/gui/tests/ClientTest.js && node source/gui/tests/LocalizationTest.js exercises the browser UI; python3 tools/tests/test_translations.py checks catalog generation.

suites.unit: source/linux/tests/UnitTest.cpp - checks of the parts that need no I/O: permission and mode parsing, masks, path handling, the transfer and synchronization planners (every word and list '-criteria=' takes, the ones it refuses, a plan refused over a file nobody could hash, and '-conflict=skip|local|remote|newer' two-way resolution), the proxy session settings, the FTP engine and TLS policy settings, the S3 object write settings and multipart upload resume state sidecar, the SSH private-key passphrase option and XML action log elements, the host-key pin spellings, the native SCP engine's connection-free parts (the shell quoting a remote path needs, the paths it refuses to send, one 'ls -l' line as an entry including a symbolic link's own name, the exact date columns of '--full-time' with the offset they are in, the rcp header lines read and written byte for byte, and the 'touch -t' stamp), the WebDAV lock-token and dead-property XML, parameter and timestamp expansion, the stored-session file and folder hierarchy helpers, the editor content-comparison and EOL normalization helpers, the file-hash and HMAC helpers, and AWS Signature Version 4 signing. Includes English/Spanish help, security messages, named-placeholder safety, locale fallback and plural-count messages.
suites.script:
source/linux/tests/ScriptTest.py - the command line and script semantics against no server: abbreviations, switches, batch modes and exit codes, local listings, help, -log and -xmllog, and stored-session password encryption (a 'savesession -password' value
written as 'lscp1$' ciphertext under sessions.key and preserved across a
re-save without the key file). The transfer presets are checked here too: the savepreset/option preset/rmspreset lifecycle, a preset stored with a site and restored when it opens, -permissions on downloads, and -rawtransfersettings validation. So are the synchronization criteria (every word and list '-criteria=' takes, the values it refuses with the names it accepts, and the two the 'both' direction cannot honour) and the raw proxy settings of 'open' and 'savesession': each upstream name applied, an unknown one refused, an incomplete or unusable proxy refused, and the password masked in the echo and in the action log. It checks -literal command input (including GUI filenames with percent placeholders), mkdir -parents argument validation, that an SSH session of either spelling (scp:// or ssh://) is served by this client's own SSH code and never asks the curl on PATH for anything - a fake curl that records every call is the witness - with a host key pin in either digest spelling compared by the client instead of handed to a library whose support cannot be known, and the adjacent -gui launcher plus Makefile/CMake source-tree launchers.
suites.live-sftp:
source/linux/tests/LiveSftpTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestSftpServer.py - refused opens (wrong password, unexpected host key), operations the server denies, an interrupted download kept in '.filepart' and its resume (automatic and with -resume), the same for an interrupted upload, a continuation that must not splice an existing destination, a stale oversized staging file, resuming across a connection that died, option resume off disabling staging, and timestamps in both directions, a synchronization whose '-criteria=checksum' sees a change the timestamp and the size hide and brings the local copy back in line, sessions carried by a SOCKS5 proxy with and without credentials (TestProxyServer.py, a wrong password refused by the proxy rather than worked around) and a stored site that keeps its proxy, and the shared stored-password format (a password encrypted by the GUI
module opening a stored session, a missing key file reported without losing
the value, and a core-written password decrypted by the GUI's reader). Recursive directory copy and multiple source files into an existing destination directory are tested over SFTP; the test server refuses the optional copy-data extension, so these prove the streamed fallback rather than the native extension. A second server mode implements copy-data and verifies the native extension path as well as exact copied bytes. The server can also refuse check-file-name, which proves the download-and-hash fallback for sha-256, sha-1, md5 and crc32, or implement the extension, which proves the native sha-256 digest and that the client does not fall back after a valid reply. It also proves that synchronize remote with a path exclusion ('-filemask=|skip/') leaves an excluded file untouched despite -delete and does not upload files from the excluded subtree. Recursive symbolic chmod is checked over a nested tree, including exact directory and file modes. copyid installs a generated OpenSSH public key into the test SFTP home, verifies the 0700/0600 permissions and proves that repeating the command does not duplicate the key. It also proves that 'etag' is refused by name on a transport with no entity tags - setting or clearing one fails and says which protocol it was asked of, '-get' answers without failing, and nothing is recorded, so the next upload of that path is an ordinary one; get/rm '-versionid' is likewise refused before any remote path is touched.
suites.live-scp: source/linux/tests/LiveScpTest.py against a throwaway OpenSSH daemon - one per test, on a port the kernel picks, with host and user keys generated for the run and public-key authentication only, so nothing outside the test's own temporary directory is read or written. It covers the native SCP engine's shell half: 'open' resolving the login's home directory and the site's initial path in one connection (and refusing a path the server will not change into), 'cd' ending where the server's shell went, listings from 'ls -l -a --full-time' with names holding spaces, hidden entries, subdirectories and symbolic links kept as links, 'stat' from 'ls -l -d' answering "missing" for a path that is not there, mkdir/chmod/mv/rm/rmdir, 'ln -s', a server-side 'cp -p', 'call' and the checksum computed from a downloaded file. Its rcp half: byte-exact downloads and uploads of a many-chunk file, an empty file and a name with spaces, a recursive tree with an empty directory and preserved directory times, '-preservetime' both ways, '-permissions' on an upload, ASCII line-ending conversion, '-speed=' pacing, and the progress percentage of an interactive run typed into a PTY. And its refusals: a host key pin checked in OpenSSH's SHA-256 spelling, as a hex digest with and without separators and as MD5, an unknown key refused in a batch run with the key printed, a wrong pin refused, resume refused by name, a stale '.filepart' discarded rather than spliced onto, an interrupted download leaving nothing under the final name, a permission the server did not grant reported in the server's own sentence, an unreachable port and a refused login reported by 'open', and a SOCKS5 proxy that really carries the session. sshd, ssh-keygen and the server's own scp binary are required; without them every case skips loudly instead of passing quietly.
suites.live-s3: source/linux/tests/LiveS3Test.py against source/linux/tests/TestS3Server.py - a throwaway S3 endpoint over TLS (the fixtures are committed) that re-derives every SigV4 signature with its own hmac/hashlib code: missing and wrong credentials refused, bucket/object CRUD, resumed downloads using HTTP byte ranges, paginated `versions` history, opaque version-ID HEAD/GET/DELETE (including delete markers), and version-specific resume staging, CopyObject for cp and rename, and a 20 MiB+123 upload checked as multipart initiation, three parts with returned ETags, completion, exact roundtrip checksum and no leftover upload. Synthetic HTTP-200 Error documents exercise CopyObject and multipart completion parsing, including abort cleanup after completion fails. Seeded pagination tests cross the 1000-entry boundary and inject repeated/missing continuation markers to prove listings fail closed rather than return partial results. The server also accepts a botocore-signed reference request. The client reaches it with curl over TLS on 127.0.0.1.
suites.gui: source/gui/tests/ClientTest.js under node with jsdom - the real Commander page booted against a stubbed backend: rendering, selection, the editor, synchronization preview and run, filename and full-text search controls/results, the site manager, terminal, queue, host-key verification, synchronized browsing (the counterpart probe, following and refusing when the other side has no such folder) and drag and drop between the panes (payload, drop-target highlight, queued upload with the dragged names, same-pane drop ignored), and browser file/folder drop enumeration with nested paths and explicit empty directories. It also checks the Explorer-style single-panel view (toggle, pane hiding, persisted choice) and the custom-commands dialog (persisted template list, save payload, explicit run confirmation and per-file run results).
suites.live-dav: source/linux/tests/LiveDavTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestDavServer.py - a throwaway WebDAV endpoint over plain HTTP with Basic challenge authentication, which also implements LOCK/UNLOCK (refusing a write from a session that holds no token with 423), PROPPATCH and dead properties, so the lock and property behavior is asserted against the server's own state rather than against the client alone: PROPFIND listings, stat with real size/time/missing-path handling, mkdir/rmdir/MOVE/DELETE, and upload/download; single-file cp uses COPY with an absolute Destination and Overwrite header, verified by a server-side operation counter and an exact readback while the source remains; a 405 refusal also verifies the streamed fallback byte-for-byte. It also checks upstream-shaped console output, aliases and transfer presets. keepuptodate uploads local files to the remote side, and a nested file arrival wakes the inotify watcher rather than waiting for the 30-second rescan. The suite is standard-library-only and needs nothing but curl. It also covers -parents mkdir and literal remote names containing spaces, percent signs, question marks and hashes through DAV PROPFIND/GET/PUT/MOVE/COPY. ETag preconditions are asserted against the server's own recorded state and its If headers: a matching tag writes, a stale one is refused with 412 and changes nothing at the destination, If-None-Match writes only where the version differs, a lock token and a tag travel in one no-tag condition list, '*' is refused rather than sent, and a precondition recorded on a collection guards that collection alone.
suites.live-curl: source/linux/tests/LiveCurlTest.py - throwaway pyftpdlib FTP, implicit FTPS and explicit-TLS (AUTH TLS) servers verify authenticated downloads/uploads and FTP .filepart completion; a recording handler proves which commands the session sent, so the suite checks that a listing is MLSD with LIST absent, that FtpUseMlsd=0 and a server refusing MLSD both fall back to LIST, that FtpUseMlsd=2 fails instead of listing without facts (and never sends LIST), and that FtpPasvMode=0 opens the data connection with PORT. The explicit-TLS case walks the TLS policy in one session: ftpes:// and Ftps=3 on an ftp:// URL, a refused handshake when the certificate is not accepted, CaCertificateFile, a PinnedPublicKey that matches, one that does not, MaxTlsVersion=1.1 refused against MinTlsVersion=1.2 accepted, and a host-key fingerprint refused with the setting to use instead. A saved site is stored and reopened by name to prove the FTP/TLS policy travels with it. No SSH protocol is served by curl any more, so none is tested here: sftp:// is LiveSftpTest.py's and scp:// is LiveScpTest.py's.

suites.gui-local: source/gui/tests/LocalWorkspaceTest.py - backend and HTTP API tests for the two-local-pane mode and for named workspaces: a local tab starts no core process and lists both directories; recursive copies and moves preserve files, timestamps and symbolic links; the ask/skip/overwrite/rename decisions, source/destination overlap refusal, second-pane CRUD, editor, checksum/search and browser drops are exercised; queue byte counts and cancellation leave no partial file; workspaces save/list/open/delete in tab order with the active tab and both pane paths, survive a failure of one tab, resolve stored sites live, and keep a credential-free private store.

!.notes: Runs the command over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection, prints its output and fails when the remote command exits non-zero, like upstream 'call'; covered by live-sftp.

ascii.notes: Sets 'option transfer ascii' like upstream, with arity checks; the conversion is applied by get/put/synchronize and was verified byte-exact against a live server. Transfer presets apply to this command - by 'option preset name', by 'savesession -preset=' when the site opens, and by the host/user/directory/mask rules when no preset was picked - with the command's own switches always winning, covered by the script suite and by an ascii preset converting a live upload.

binary.notes: Sets 'option transfer binary' like upstream, with arity checks. Transfer presets apply to this command - by 'option preset name', by 'savesession -preset=' when the site opens, and by the host/user/directory/mask rules when no preset was picked - with the command's own switches always winning, covered by the script suite and by an ascii preset converting a live upload.

bye.notes: Stops the script where it stands with no output and no arguments, like upstream's continue flag (exit, quit and end are the same command, bye an alias of exit). Covered by the script suite.

call.notes: Rejoins and re-quotes the arguments, runs them over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection (the main SFTP session stays open) and fails when the remote command exits non-zero; covered by live-sftp.

cd.notes: With no argument it goes to the home directory captured at connect time; either form prints the resulting directory, like upstream (upstream's script interpreter has no directory history either). Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

checksum.notes: For the four documented algorithms (sha-256, sha-1, md5, crc32), returns the lowercase digest and remote path. On SFTP it asks the check-file-name extension first for supported algorithms and falls back to downloading and hashing when the server declines; covered by live-sftp for all four fallback digests and the native sha-256 reply.

chmod.notes: Octal and symbolic modes ('u+x', 'a=r,go-w', 'u+s', 'X') and -recursive over a directory tree, symbolic links skipped; the mode is checked before the connection so a typo is reported even when offline. Upstream's script command passes an octal string only, so the symbolic forms and recursion are an extension; recursive octal and symbolic modes are covered by unit and live-sftp.

close.notes: Closes the session with no argument or with the 1-based index of the session to close ('close 1' is the only index that exists here), prints "Session '<name>' closed." like upstream, and refuses other indexes; like upstream it needs a connection before the argument is even looked at. Opening a different stored site closes the previous connection the same way. Covered by the script suite (offline refusal) and the live WebDAV suite.

copyid.notes: Reads the session's private key or a supplied OpenSSH public/private key or PPK v2/v3 key, then appends its authorized_keys line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, creating the directory 0700 and the file 0600 and leaving an already installed key alone. PPK files are parsed natively and their MAC is verified; -passphrase= supports encrypted keys. Needs an sftp:// or scp:// session; covered by live-sftp with public and encrypted private keys, exact ~/.ssh and authorized_keys permissions, and duplicate suppression.

cp.notes: Remote copy is checked through native SFTP copy-data when the server implements it, streamed SFTP fallback when it does not, WebDAV COPY (and streamed fallback on refusal), and S3 CopyObject. Recursive trees, multiple sources into an existing directory, overwrite refusal in batch mode, and explicit overwrite with confirm off are covered by the live-sftp, live-dav and live-s3 suites.

dir.notes: Alias of 'ls' with the same listing, mask and no-match semantics. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

echo.notes: Plain token output. The line has already been through the upstream expansions - script parameters, %TIMESTAMP% and environment variables - because they are applied before dispatch; text in single quotes is left alone. Covered by the script suite.

exit.notes: Stops the script where it stands with no output and no arguments, like upstream's continue flag. Covered by the script suite.

get.notes: Binary, ASCII and automatic transfers with WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks, size and time criteria), `-filemask=`, option include/exclude and failonnomatch. Resume is binary-only and is rejected with ASCII. Also `-resumesupport=on|off|<KB>`, `-append` (native SFTP only), `-speed=<KB/s>`, `-neweronly`/`-noneweronly`, `-preservetime[=all]`, `-permissions[=mode]` and `-rawtransfersettings[=N]`, which refuses by name any setting this build does not apply. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's `.filepart` name and move onto the destination only when complete. `option resume automatic` (the default) stages binary files of 100 KB or more, `on` stages all, and `off` none. Transfer presets apply (see `option`). S3 `-versionid=<ID>` downloads one exact object version; its resumable staging suffix is derived from the ID so concurrent/historical versions cannot share partial data. A version switch is refused on non-S3 transports before touching paths. Covered by the script, live-DAV, live-S3 and live-SFTP suites.

help.notes: 'help' lists every command as upstream does, name in an 8-wide column followed by its one-line description; 'help <command>' prints that command's help text, and aliases resolve to the command they stand for (unknown names are refused). Covered by the script suite.

keepuptodate.notes: Takes no direction word; like upstream it reflects changes in the local directory onto the remote one. Accepts -delete, -filemask=, -transfer=, -interval=, -count= and -continue (keeps watching after a failed pass). A recursive inotify watcher starts another pass on local changes; -interval= remains a full-rescan safety net, with timer polling if the watch cannot be set up. Covered by unit, live-dav and live-sftp.

lcd.notes: Changes the local directory and prints the directory it landed in, like upstream; a directory that cannot be entered is an error and stops a batch script. Covered by the script suite.

lls.notes: Upstream's columns: date, time, size (or <DIR> for a directory) and the name, with the date and time widths fitted to the widest entry; a trailing wildcard leaf masks the listing, the default lists everything, and a path that matches nothing prints the no-match sentence - a failure only under option failonnomatch. Covered by the script suite.

ln.notes: SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link) and explicit refusal on protocols without symlinks, covered by live-sftp and live-dav.

lpwd.notes: Prints the local working directory, no arguments like upstream. Covered by the script suite.

ls.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format prints the entry's listing line - the server's long name over SFTP, a synthesized ls -l line on the transfer backends - which is what upstream prints as well (File->ListingStr). A mask that matches nothing prints the no-match sentence, a failure only under option failonnomatch. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.

man.notes: Same as 'help': the two-column listing without arguments, the per-command help text with one, aliases resolving to their command. Covered by the script suite.

mget.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mkdir.notes: Creates exactly one directory - one argument like upstream - and is silent on success; refusals (a name that exists) and other server answers are reported and fail the script. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.

mput.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mv.notes: Multi-source with an existing-directory target, rename in place and confirm-on-overwrite, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

open.notes: URL sessions and stored-session names (including folder/site paths), -passphrase= for encrypted SSH keys, -hostkey= verification and '-rawsettings[=N] NAME=VALUE...' for proxy, FTP/TLS and S3 object settings; unknown settings and unusable proxies are refused by name before connecting, and passwords/passphrases are redacted in echo and XML logs. Covered by script, live-sftp, live-s3 and live-curl.

option.notes: echo, batch (on/off/abort/continue), confirm, resume, transfer (binary/ascii/automatic), include/exclude (one mask, setting either clears the other, 'clear' resets), synchdelete, failonnomatch, reconnecttime (seconds or off, with automatic reconnect), editor, editmaxsize, and a listing when called with no name. Option and value names may be abbreviated when the abbreviation is unambiguous; masks, programs and numbers are never abbreviated. 'option preset <name>' selects a transfer preset for the following transfers, 'option preset off' disables presets for the session and a missing preset name fails loudly; 'savesession -preset=' persists the preset with the site, which loads it when opened, both directions covered by the script suite and the live WebDAV preset roundtrip.

put.notes: Binary, ASCII and automatic transfers with WinSCP file masks, `-filemask=`, option include/exclude and failonnomatch, `-permissions=`/`-nopermissions`, and the `-resume`, `-append`, `-speed=`, `-resumesupport=`, `-neweronly`/`-noneweronly` and `-preservetime[=all]` switches of `get`. Append and resume are mutually exclusive and need the native SFTP transport. Transfer presets apply (see `option`), and `-rawtransfersettings[=N]` refuses by name any setting this build cannot apply. Resume-capable transfers stage through `.filepart` and move onto the destination only when complete. `option resume automatic` (the default) stages binary files of 100 KB or more, `on` stages all, and `off` none. Setting permissions on the server needs native SFTP, so `-permissions` on an upload is not applied over curl. Covered by the script and live-DAV suites.

pwd.notes: Prints the remote working directory after checking there is a session, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

recv.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

rename.notes: One source and one destination only, like upstream's mv in its rename form. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

rm.notes: Multiple files, masks and -onlyfile (directories are skipped with a status), no-match reporting gated by option failonnomatch, like upstream. No recursive delete, matching upstream. The LinSCP S3 extension `-versionid=<ID>` removes only the named version or delete marker, refused by name on non-S3 transports and covered by live-S3 and live-SFTP.

rmdir.notes: Multiple directories in one command, continuing past failures; only empty directories, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

send.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

session.notes: Upstream 'session' semantics: it needs an open session, no argument lists the open sessions as '%3d name' and prints which one is active, and 'session <index>' switches (only index 1 exists with one connection; other indexes are refused). The stored-sites listing, export/import and lookup by name moved to the plural 'sessions' command, which savesession/rmsession feed and 'open <name>' also resolves. The session folder tree and raw settings are not part of this command and stay tracked under 'open'. Covered by the script suite (the offline refusals) and the live WebDAV suite (listing, switching).

stat.notes: Prints the one listing line upstream prints for the path (the line 'ls -l' shows: permissions, links, owner, group, size, time and name), exactly one line with no key/value text. features.name: SCP

Host keys are checked by the same code as for `sftp://`. The protocol cannot continue a partial transfer: a resume is refused by name, and a staging file left by an interrupted run is discarded rather than spliced onto. linscp_additions.name: etag
linscp_additions.notes: 'etag <file> -match=ETAG | -nomatch=ETAG' records an If-Match or If-None-Match precondition with the session, '-get' asks the server for the path's ETag with a Depth-0 PROPFIND and prints it, and '-clear' forgets a recorded one. A recorded precondition travels in the If header of every later upload, delete and move of that path, in the same condition list as a lock token, and the tag is re-quoted on the way out because the command splitter has already taken the quotes 'etag -get' printed off it. Exactly one action per call is required, '*' is refused rather than sent as a tag nothing matches, and a session whose protocol has no ETags - the SSH engines, FTP, S3 - is refused by name instead of recording a precondition nothing would compare. The If header it produces, the tag it refuses, the 412 a stale one earns and the refusal on a protocol with no entity tags are covered by unit, live-dav and live-sftp; dav.etag-preconditions is the capability row.

Covered by live-s3.

capabilities.notes: Native libssh SFTP session refuses bad credentials and unexpected SSH host keys.
Transfers, directories, renames, symbolic links (ln/symlink) and chmod use native SFTP requests rather than curl.
Native copy-data replies are used when offered; a multi-source/recursive streamed fallback works when absent.
Server check-file-name is used for sha-256 and all documented hashes fall back to downloaded bytes when refused.
Octal and recursive symbolic chmod plus file and directory timestamp preservation (-preservetime=all) work against the live SFTP server.

The id is the row's history: an scp:// transfer is not curl's any more. The bytes go over an SSH exec channel running the server's own 'scp -f' and 'scp -t', with the rcp wire protocol spoken by the client - a timestamp header, a mode/size/name header, exactly the stated bytes and an acknowledgement per step, in both directions. Downloads stage through '.filepart' and are renamed when whole, uploads carry '-permissions' and '-preservetime', a tree goes through the recursive form of the protocol with an 'E' per closed level, and continuing a partial file is refused by name instead of attempted, because the protocol has no offset to continue from. ASCII conversion, masks, speed limits, progress and the interrupt behavior are the shared transfer path's and are checked here as well.

The directory engine runs `ls -l -a --full-time` in its own SSH connection and parses it with the shared long-listing parser: `.` and `..` are skipped, names with spaces are kept whole, symbolic links keep their link type, and dates are read with the offset the server prints them in. `stat` is `ls -l -d`, so a missing path is reported as missing. `cd` is `cd <path> && pwd`, so the working directory is the one the server actually entered. `open` resolves the home directory and the site's initial path in one command. A server whose `ls` has no `--full-time` and no `env` gets the plainer command rather than an error.

The commands upstream runs on the remote shell, and the metadata a shell can set that 'ls -l' can read back: mkdir, rmdir, rm (never '-f', so a path that is not there stays an error the server words), mv, chmod with the mode the script parsed, 'cp -p' for a server-side copy - with a server that has no 'cp' answered by streaming through the client instead - 'ln -s' for a symbolic link, 'touch -t' asked for in UTC for a modification time, and the rcp timestamp header for the time a transfer carries. Every path is quoted for a POSIX shell and a path holding a control character is refused instead of being sent, because a newline in a name cannot be told apart from the end of a listing line. A refusal arrives as the sentence the server printed, 'call' hands the rest of the line to that shell, and 'checksum' says plainly that the digest came from a downloaded file, this protocol having no server-side hashing to ask for.
curl handles authenticated FTP/FTPS downloads and uploads with .filepart staging and PTY progress reporting against live FTP and FTPS servers.

Plain FTP is served by the native FTP engine, which asks for MLSD where the server advertises it: size, type, time and permissions come from the protocol instead of from an ls -l line each server formats its own way. MLST answers stat, a server that refuses MLSD falls back to LIST, FtpUseMlsd=0 asks for LIST from the start, and FtpUseMlsd=2 (require) fails the listing rather than returning one without the machine-readable facts. The ls -l parser is shared with the curl backend, which serves the LIST replies and every transfer.

FtpPasvMode picks the data connection the native engine opens: passive by default, EPSV first with PASV as the fallback, and FtpPasvMode=0 opens it from the client instead, binding a listener and telling the server where it is with PORT or EPRT. FtpForcePasvIp decides whose address a PASV reply may use - 0 the control connection's, 1 (the default) the reply's unless it is unroutable, 2 the reply verbatim - and FtpAccount answers a server that asks for an account name on top of the credentials.

FTPS stays on curl, the TLS client of this build, and upstream's setting names drive it: ftps:// (Ftps=1) is implicit TLS on port 990, ftpes:// (Ftps=2 or 3 on an ftp:// URL) is explicit TLS through --ssl-reqd, MinTlsVersion and MaxTlsVersion become --tlsv1.x and --tls-max, TlsCertificateFile and TlsCertificateKeyFile become --cert and --key, CaCertificateFile and CaCertificateDir become --cacert and --capath, and PinnedPublicKey becomes --pinnedpubkey. A policy curl cannot honour, or one given to a protocol without TLS, is refused before the connection rather than dropped; hostkey='*' is the only value that turns certificate validation off.
Depth 0/1 PROPFIND parses collection type, size and modification time; stat distinguishes absent paths.
MKCOL, PUT, GET, DELETE and refusal of nonempty collection removal work against the live server.
MOVE and COPY send absolute Destination URIs; a refused COPY falls back to a byte-exact stream.
curl URL paths, DAV href comparisons and Destination headers preserve spaces and literal %, ? and # in names.

'lock <file> [-timeout=SECONDS]' takes an exclusive write lock and keeps its token in the session; 'unlock <file>' releases it. Every later upload, delete and move of that path carries the token as the If header, so a second writer without it is refused with 423 and the locked file keeps its content. A server that does not implement LOCK answers 405 and the command prints that instead of reporting a protected write. Upstream's WebDAV backend sends no LOCK or UNLOCK at all, so this is a LinSCP extension.

'property <file> -set=NAME=VALUE' stores one dead property through PROPPATCH and 'property <file> -get=NAME' reads it back with a named-property PROPFIND; both use this client's own namespace (urn:linscp:properties), a name that would build invalid XML is refused before any request, and a property the server does not have prints 'NAME is not set' rather than failing. The conditional write is the lock token: PUT, DELETE and MOVE of a locked path send If, which is what makes the server refuse a write whose lock is gone (423).
Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4; absent or incorrect credentials fail against a TLS verifier.
ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2, HEAD and virtual directories are exercised against the test endpoint; malformed or repeated pagination state is an error rather than a partial directory listing.

capabilities.notes: Native SFTP refuses an unknown/unexpected host key until it is pinned.

`-hostkey=` accepts the fingerprint spellings people paste: SHA-256 in hex (with or without `:`), `SHA256:base64`, curl's `sha256//base64`, and MD5 with or without the `MD5:` marker `ssh-keygen` prints. Both SSH engines compare it with the fingerprint the SSH core reports, so `sftp://` and `scp://` pins share one code path, and no pin depends on the installed curl. A key that does not match is refused. An unknown key in a run nobody can answer is refused with the key printed so it can be pinned, and a checked key is remembered. A TLS session keeps chain validation (the system store, or CaCertificateFile and CaCertificateDir) and pins the server's public key with `--pinnedpubkey`. A value curl cannot compare is refused, and only `*` disables the checks.
SFTP SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT proxies and curl proxy routing are verified live; wrong proxy credentials and unsupported proxy modes are refused rather than bypassed.

Scoped native SSH jump-host support: Tunnel=1 plus TunnelHostName/PortNumber/UserName/Password/PublicKeyFile/Passphrase/HostKey creates an authenticated direct-tcpip channel for an SFTP/SCP/SSH destination. A private close-on-exec socket pair, not a TCP listener, joins the independent transports. The jump resolves the destination, inherits the proxy and has its own credentials/key check; destination keys retain their original host/port identity. Passwords/passphrases are encrypted at rest when explicitly saved, masked in logs, absent from GUI process arguments/status and isolated per child environment. The GUI offers separate key challenges and credential-saving controls; queued operations and -shell retain the tunnel. Tests exercise exact bytes, refusals, interrupted staging and cleanup. This does not claim GSSAPI or non-SSH tunnel support. Changed keys have an explicit warning; per-hop Remember choices persist independently, without saving transient credentials or globally caching a tab-only pin. Slow/backpressured I/O, forwarding timeout and process cancellation are covered too. TunnelPasswordPlain/TunnelPassphrasePlain aliases are accepted, encrypted at rest and censored in logs; this is not encrypted WinSCP password import. Exec/shell callbacks retain output and exit status through coalesced channel/transport closure, but only publish a status after authenticated EOF/close; repeated direct/tunneled stdout/stderr/exit-7 and deliberately truncated-status fixtures cover this boundary.

The XML action log (-xmllog=) writes the upstream session format (http://winscp.net/schema/session/1.0): '<group>' per command and structured '<upload>', '<download>', '<rm>', '<mkdir>', '<mv>', '<cp>', '<chmod>', '<touch>', '<call>', '<ls>', '<stat>', '<checksum>' and '<cwd>' elements with '<result success>' children and secrets masked. No WinSCP .NET assembly or equivalent object model for Linux. The C ABI header the Windows port left behind (source/linux/liblinscp.h) is gone: it declared a library that no build produced, and a public header for an API that does not exist is worse than none. The gap is unchanged - the automation object model still has to be built.
capabilities.gap: Define an API contract and test automation clients; a CLI is not the assembly.
acceptance: Define the Linux object-model contract and upstream compatibility boundary. Build and test an actual .NET library for session lifecycle, listing, transfer, synchronization, cancellation, structured results and error propagation. A subprocess helper alone is not assembly parity.

capabilities.notes: automation/LinSCP.psm1 is a PowerShell 7 (pwsh) module that wraps the console client in -server mode and exports Open-LScpSession, Close-LScpSession, Get-LScpItem, Send-LScpItem, Get-LScpDirectory and Sync-LScpDirectory; 'make install', 'cmake --install' and the Debian package all put it in PREFIX/share/linscp/automation. Passwords travel on stdin to -server, never on a command line. The test harness (automation/test_psmodule.py, run by make check-live, CTest and CI) has static checks that always run and a Pester suite (automation/LinSCP.Tests.ps1, invoked through automation/Invoke-LinSCPPester.ps1 so Pester 4 and Pester 5 both run) against the throwaway WebDAV endpoint: a session opened and closed, an upload and a download of exact bytes, a missing file reported without throwing, a listing as pipeline objects, terminating errors, a timeout-cancelled connection, and a password that appears neither in the process list nor in any output. The live cases ran green in CI (the 'PowerShell module regressions' step of the Makefile job, e.g. master run 39291584018), and that step now fails unless its evidence line reports ran>=1 skipped=0 failed=0 and Pester reports total>=1 skipped=0, so a future skip cannot look green. The module remains a compatibility module over the CLI rather than upstream's assembly API; the assembly itself is automation.dotnet.

capabilities.notes: A desktop session is recognised as Wayland or as X11 before anything is asked of it, and only a program that can draw on it is started. The console client finds the compositor by its socket in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR - the default 'wayland-0' when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is not exported, so a session started by a launcher or a user service is still found - and refuses a Wayland-only terminal under X11, where it exits before mapping a window, while an X11-only one under Wayland is a reported XWayland fallback rather than a silent choice. The graphical client draws no window itself and asks the desktop's own URI launcher ($BROWSER, xdg-open, gio) for a browser, which needs no X11 and no window manager of the X11 kind; linscp.desktop starts it with that option and does not claim a startup notification it could never complete. Covered by unit, gui-desktop-uri and wayland-compatibility; no case runs against a live compositor, so the interaction with one is not certified here.

No system file-manager shell commands or upstream extension system. The half-translated Nautilus extension the Windows Explorer integration left behind is gone: it ran no session, so it uploaded nothing, and it was neither installed nor documented. The command templates of the graphical client (source/gui/explorer-commands.json) are its own feature and are shipped by all three installers.
capabilities.gap: Specify desired desktop environment integrations and build/test them individually.
acceptance: Specify supported file managers and extension API. Add explicit, opt-in installation and removal, selection transport without shell interpolation, confirmation and extension permission boundaries. Test packaged installation as well as source-tree execution.

acceptance: Ship a catalog for every language the project claims to support and translate the whole interface into it, starting with the languages the upstream project already ships.
Add a test that walks the catalogs and reports the messages of the client that are still answered in English, so a new interface string cannot slip through untranslated.

LinSCP is a Linux-only client and the check that says so is part of the build: tools/check_platform_conversion.py reads the client's own sources and refuses a Windows API call, a Windows header, a Windows-only compilation branch, a Windows environment variable, a Windows executable, a Windows path, a file of another platform, an installer that does not ship what the other installers ship, and an error message whose operation phrase contradicts the template it is filled into. It runs in 'make -C source/linux check', as the CTest case 'platform-conversion-check', and in CI. The vendored xterm.js files under source/gui/web/vendor are upstream code and are not scanned; everything else in the tree is this project's own.

Shared LIST parser handles Unix long listings, DOS/IIS listings (MM-DD-YY[YY] HH:MM[AM|PM] <DIR>/size with spaces in names, date/size variants) and VMS listings (name;version size DD-MON-YYYY HH:MM:SS [OWNER] (RWED,RWED,RE,RE) with directory detection via .DIR extension and protection-field permissions). MLSD provides machine-readable alternative; DOS/VMS malformed-input is rejected and treated as empty rather than silently succeeding, and LIST fallback is exercised against live servers that emit the supported formats. Other non-Unix dialects remain undocumented as unsupported.

'etag <file> -match=ETAG' records an If-Match precondition and '-nomatch=ETAG' an If-None-Match one, per path and per session; '-get' reads the current tag with a Depth-0 PROPFIND and tells a missing path apart from a server that reported no tag; '-clear' forgets a recorded one. A WebDAV upload, delete or move of that path carries the tag in the If header, in one no-tag condition list together with a lock token when the path is also locked - '(<opaquelocktoken:...> ["tag"])' - because RFC 4918 reads an If header as either no-tag lists or tagged lists and never as both, and the token has to be the Coded-URL of angle brackets a standard server looks for. '-nomatch=' is sent as '(Not ["tag"])': a list without the Not would have been If-Match, the opposite of the documented 'write only if the version differs'. The value travels quoted as the entity tag the server gave - 'etag -get' prints "abc", the command splitter strips those quotes, and DavEntityTag puts them back with a W/ weakness prefix left outside them - and '*' is refused by name instead of sent, since an If header has no way to say 'only if absent' and a quoted asterisk is a tag no resource carries, which would guard nothing while looking like a guard. DAV response text is XML-unescaped on the way in, so an escaped getetag arrives as the tag it is rather than as '"..."', which no precondition could ever match. Against a live server a matching tag writes, a stale one is refused with 412 and leaves the destination's bytes and its collection listing exactly as they were, If-None-Match writes where the version differs and is refused where it does not, an absent resource answers it, and a 412 on MOVE says which of its two causes it was rather than always blaming an existing destination. Collection semantics are defined rather than inherited: a precondition guards the path it was recorded for and nothing below it, because a collection's tag names its listing - the first member written under an inherited one would stale it and fail every later write in that directory. A session whose protocol has no entity tags (the SSH engines, FTP, S3) is refused by name, '-get' included, rather than left believing a later write is conditional. Upstream's WebDAV backend sends no ETag precondition at all, so this is a LinSCP extension.

`versions` lists exact-key or prefix history and delete markers through guarded ListObjectVersions pagination; `get -versionid=` reads one version, HEAD metadata handles delete markers, and resumable staging uses an ID-specific suffix; `rm -versionid=` deletes only the named version/marker. Live tests cover opaque query characters, a 1001-record two-page history plus missing/repeated pagination-marker refusals, historical/current downloads, isolated resume staging and marker creation/removal without losing other versions.

CLI editing supports explicit legacy-encoding selection via iconv (ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, EUC-JP, Shift-JIS, UTF-16 etc.): 'edit -encoding=ENC' converts between the file's encoding and UTF-8, round-tripping byte-exact fixtures with BOM/EOL preservation, and rejects invalid sequences or unrepresentable output without silent replacement. Browser editor/search remain UTF-8-only and reject binary/non-UTF-8 files with an explicit message; the encoding contract is documented and tested.

The XML action log (-xmllog=) now writes the upstream session format instead of a look-alike: root '<session xmlns="http://winscp.net/schema/session/1.0" name="user@host"|site|nosession start="...Z">', one '<group>' per script command named by its masked line (grouping is always on, so a continuous reader knows a command finished when its group closes), one element per physical operation - upload, download (both with '<size>'), rm (including rmdir and S3 exact-version removal), mkdir, mv, cp, chmod ('<permissions>' as 'rwxr-xr-x' letters), touch ('<modification>'), call ('<output>'/'<erroroutput>' streams and '<exitcode>' from a captured run), ls ('<files>' of '<file>' with the upper-case type character), stat (one '<file>' with no '<filename>'), checksum ('<algorithm>'/'<checksum>') and cwd - each ending in '<result success="true|false">' with '<message>' on failure, and a '<failure>' with the command's masked errors closing a failed group. Attribute and text escaping follow upstream's XmlAttributeEscape/XmlEscape pair (newline as '
' in attributes, CR and unrepresentable controls dropped), timestamps are the one UTC '....NNNZ' spelling. The format is pinned in the repository as docs/winscp-session-1.0.xsd, written from upstream's emitter (source/core/SessionInfo.cpp) and its XML Logging documentation. The script suite validates the shipped fixtures (fixtures/xml/) and freshly produced logs against that schema with xmlschema - including a masked-password failure - and reads operations back the way an upstream-style consumer does; the live SFTP suite validates a full real session log the same way and checks every action element's parameters against the bytes it moved. Boundaries kept: console output is not recorded (as upstream), operations with no upstream element (symlink creation) are absent (as upstream), 'difference' elements for a bare synchronization comparison are schema-defined but only emitted through the transfer/mkdir/rm elements a synchronization actually performs, and a run that never connects keeps the upstream fallback session name 'nosession'.

A local-to-local session is a tab whose protocol is 'local' and which names two absolute local directories (the upstream IsLocalBrowser/OtherLocalDirectory shape). CoreSession.start, connect and alive never spawn the core and never open a socket; the right pane lists its directory through the same API the remote pane uses. Copies and moves are planned and run in-process on the queue with byte progress and cancellation: recursive trees, merge into an existing directory, atomic per-file replacement through a temporary file, timestamps and modes preserved, symbolic links copied as links, and ask/skip/overwrite/rename decisions (the browser answers 'ask' once and retries). Source equal to or inside the destination is refused before queueing. The second pane also supports mkdir, rename, delete, chmod, properties, checksums, editor save and find. The server-only terminal, synchronization and remote transfer dialogs are not offered in this mode.

Named workspaces are stored in workspaces.json beside sessions.ini (0600, fsynced and atomically replaced) and restore the tabs in order with the saved active tab and both pane paths. An entry is either a local tab with its two directories or a remote tab; a tab that came from a stored site records only the site name and is resolved from sessions.ini on every open, so the site's password encryption, pinned host key and tunnel policy stay authoritative. An ad-hoc tab is saved as a snapshot with password, tunnel password, tunnel passphrase and site name removed. Each tab opens independently: a deleted or renamed site, a missing local directory or a host-key challenge is reported in 'failed' without stopping the others, and a challenge is parked in the normal host-key table for the user to verify. A local site can be saved directly, since the console client has no local transport.

scope.definition: Inventory of the pinned upstream script registrations, Linux additions, reviewed feature areas and known implementation/compatibility gaps. Completeness of this ledger is not full WinSCP feature parity or an exhaustive behavioral/security certification.
limitations: Verified means the stated scoped behavior has named automated evidence, not every upstream variant.
Source/test citations record where evidence is defined, not a claim that every suite ran in this workspace.
Mock-server/browser fixtures do not certify every real server, browser, file manager or architecture.
Missing capabilities are retained and must not be deleted to pass the full-parity gate.

The Wayland and X11 behavior is established from the sources, from fixtures that say which display server this is, and from a check that refuses the X11-only shapes; no case in this ledger runs against a live compositor, so a real Wayland session is not certified by it.
scope.conversion: LinSCP ships on Linux alone. The Windows port was removed in 1.0-2 and this audit looked for what it left behind: the script command splitter still read a backslash as an escape inside double quotes, so a path carried over from a Windows client lost its separators; the error messages still carried the Windows wording of an operation phrase, so the template said a preposition twice; the tree still held a public C ABI header with no library behind it and a half-translated file-manager extension that could not run; and the three installers disagreed about what an installation contains. All four are fixed, and tools/check_platform_conversion.py now keeps them fixed.
scope.wayland: A Linux desktop runs on Wayland or on X11, and the way an application gets that wrong is silent: it asks for $DISPLAY, finds nothing on a session that exports $WAYLAND_DISPLAY and no X server at all, and reports that the user has no desktop. LinSCP draws no window of its own, so this is about the three times it asks the desktop for something - the terminal window 'terminal' opens, the browser window the graphical client asks the desktop to show, and the desktop entry that starts it. tools/check_wayland_compatibility.py keeps them session-aware, and refuses X11-only and Wayland-only helper programs outright, so that neither display server is a privileged case here.
